source: test fixture — issue #238 item 1: one substance whose route-QUALIFIED row is the only one a question's own word resolves, while the ANSWER's wording reaches the unqualified row that canonicalRow then elects
description: The two Estrone sulfate rows are ONE substance (both publish substanceName 'estrone sulfate', and the curated schema derives the rest of the key from the display stem, which strips '(topical)'), but only the QUALIFIED row lists the bare alias 'estrone' — so a question saying 'estrone' resolves that row ALONE while an answer saying 'estrone sulfate' reaches the unqualified one. canonicalRow's first rung then elects the unqualified row, so the subject moves between the pre-answer pass and the chips pass: the asymmetry runs the OPPOSITE way to drug-reference-charted-substance-row.json, whose bare alias sits on the unqualified row and where the answer therefore cannot move the subject. The alias asymmetry is posed in a shape the production loader leaves alone: every row lists its own display name among its aliases, so DrugReferenceValidity.sanitizeAliases (which would otherwise add it back, ENTRY_NOT_NAMED_BY_ITS_OWN_ALIASES / REPAIRED) is a strict no-op and the premise is true of a real load rather than only of the setEntries seam. The two rows publish DIFFERENT daily ceilings (3000 for the qualified row against 2000 for the unqualified one) so a dose case can say which row's ceiling was quoted, and Warfarin is here only to be the interacting active order that lets one response carry an interaction chip. The two Norethisterone rows are a SECOND substance, in play only because the ANSWER names it — the question does not and the patient is not on it — so it is the one shape SubstanceSubjects has no pass-invariant group for, and it exists to pin that the fallback FOLDS those rows rather than keeping whichever reached the arm first (issue #206's property inside one pass). Its rows publish the same bare alias on purpose, so the answer resolves both, Its ATC code is kept in a different level-4 subgroup from the estrone rows for readability only: measured by mutation, giving the two families one subgroup reddens nothing, because no arm in this arrangement compares two in-play drugs.

interactions.note: Major. Oestrogens oppose warfarin's anticoagulant effect; check the INR.
Moderate. Progestogens may alter warfarin's effect; check the INR.
